articles.description:
As we make the seasonal switch from flip-flops to flannel, it’s only natural that our thoughts on food follow suit, with cooling cocktails and simple salads giving way to cozy casseroles and belly-warming baked goods. And right now, the shelves at your neighborhood Trader Joe’s are positively brimming with fall-forward, limited edition products imbued with the likes of pumpkin, apple, & maple (oh my!), as well as everyday favorites with a fall feel, like our Spiced Chai Black Tea Concentrate.

Brewed with filtered water and steeped in small batches to fully develop its characteristic flavors—namely, allspice, black pepper, cardamom, clove, cinnamon, and ginger—this Black Tea Concentrate wholly embodies the spirit of coziness for which fall is so famed. It’s the ideal base for a perfectly perfumed, satisfyingly sweet, and altogether tasty Spiced Chai latte. You might try it in your oatmeal for an unabashed burst of spice and sweetness. We like to use it as the not-so-secret ingredient in our recipe for Spiced Chai Apple Crisp. Watch the recipe video below or read the instructions that follow for a sweet nod to the abundance of the season…

heroImage.alt: Casserole dish of Spiced Chai Apple Crisp alongside two bowls of crisp topped with whipped cream & caramel sauce, next to a bottle of Trader Joe's Spiced Chai Black Tea Concentrate

articles.title: Fall Forward With Spiced Chai Apple Crisp

articles.description:
Brunch is the best! Unless you’re the one charged with producing a variety of hot and ready brunchables. Then it can seem like a daunting task, even for just a few family members or friends. Thankfully, with a little help from Trader Joe’s, you can still have a bang-up brunch that’s honestly easy-breezy to prepare.

Read on to discover what little time and effort it takes to heat the five, brunchy Trader Joe’s products highlighted below—and get a 'taste' of what it’s like to eat each one. Once you decide on your menu, hop on over to your neighborhood store and grab what you need to host your own mid-morning meal in celebration of spring!

articles.description:
These days, everyone’s feeling a little short on hugs. While some are antsy for another hug from Grandma, others are missing the feeling of that once commonplace embrace between good friends. Couldn’t we all use another hug right now?

Trader Joe’s doesn’t sell hugs. We sell food. And, food is like a hug—specifically, there is warmth and satisfaction to be had getting your mouth around a fork filled with your favorite food. Of all the cherished products in our stores that customers hold close to their hearts, we chose a few we think best embody an eatable embrace. (We’re sure you can think of many more.)

Consider the video and words below as a sort of digital cuddle—from us, to you. And, while food-hugs are better enjoyed in the company of huggable others, for now, we can at least cling to the notion that such shared meals are still ahead!
articles.title: Foods Like A Hug

articles.description:
Planning a barbecue, cookout, or picnic can be a perplexing process. There’s just so much to consider! First there’s the location, then things like the decorations, the music, what to wear, activities, and especially the food. Of course, Trader Joe’s has all the mains, sides, condiments, desserts, and beverages you could possibly want—but how do you decide which of our grill-worthy grub and sun-ready snacks will best serve your BBQ? 

To solve this summer conundrum, we recommend a trip to your neighborhood Trader Joe’s—but first, answer these five personality-related questions below. While the specific nature of these BBQs & As may appear to beat around the bush, just trust us—our quiz has been constructed with a sophisticated formula that pairs your particular personality and preferences with the Trader Joe’s products that will spell success in all your cookout endeavors!
articles.title: BBQ & A - Discover Your Cookout Character

articles.description:
Throughout Mexico and in cities across the U.S., street vendors sell mouthwatering, well-seasoned corn on the cob known as elote. While the fixins may vary some from vendor to vendor, elote typically comes slathered in mayo or crema, rolled in grated Parmesan or cotija cheese, dusted with chili powder, and squirted with lime juice. As anyone who grew up visiting the neighborhood elotero or making elote at home can tell you, it’s a highly crave-able combination of flavors that leaves a life-long impression.

Elotes are already pretty darn portable (they’re usually served on sticks), but last year, we upped the ante on port-elote-ability with Trader Joe’s Organic Elote Corn Chip Dippers. Suddenly, customers could enjoy all of that corny, creamy, spiced elote goodness… in a chip! The product’s popularity was unprecedented. Which got us thinking… What other foods could use an elote infusion? Then, like an Everything Bagel in the mist, innovation revealed itself: let folks decide for themselves when & how to add the elote!

In the spirit of our Everything But the Bagel Sesame Seasoning Blend that came before it, Trader Joe’s Everything But the Elote Seasoning Blend is "Everything" you might find on elote—chile pepper, Parmesan cheese, chipotle powder, cumin, dried cilantro, sea salt, etc.—minus the corn itself. (We also add some corn flour & cane sugar, so there’s no mistaking what this stuff is meant to mimic!)

You’ll find new Trader Joe’s Everything But the Elote Seasoning Blend sitting in our spice section, for $2.49 per 2.3-ounce jar. Once you road test the recipes below, we suspect we’ll find it sitting in your spice section, too… permanently. ¡Disfruta!

heroImage.alt: kaleidescope background of colorful ears of corn and popcorn kernels; TJ’s Everything But the Elote Seasoning Blend package on top

articles.title: We Like It. We Like It Elote.
